Subject: VectorForge — Dedicated sizing worksheet and traffic profile request

Hi Marta — great to meet yesterday. As discussed, to give you a tight Dedicated capacity proposal we need a short, focused traffic/profile worksheet. I attached a single-sheet CSV example for token histograms and a lightweight prompt/response matrix (see vectorforge_token_histogram.csv) — if you can paste the numbers below or attach exported telemetry that would be perfect.

High-priority fields we need (short):
- Peak concurrent sessions (peak minute, peak 5-min)
- Average and 95/99th prompt length (tokens) and response length distribution
- Percent of calls that use streaming vs batch (streaming affects socket concurrency)
- Session shape: average prompts per session and median session duration
- Dayparting: peak hour % of daily traffic, expected weekly variability
- Model preference/fallbacks (e.g., mix of gpt-like, embeddings, rerank)
- KV-cache hit estimate if you have it (or % of calls that can be cached)
- SLO targets (p95 latency target for first token and p99 overall)

If you prefer, we can run a quick Zoom and capture the telemetry live — otherwise a pasted table here is fine. Targeting a first-cut Dedicated sizing by EOB Thursday.

Best,
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@vectorforge.ai>

Subject: Re: VectorForge — Dedicated sizing worksheet and traffic profile request

Thanks Karthik — pasted answers below (exported a small histogram attached as vectorforge_token_histogram.csv). Let me know if anything needs clarification.

- Peak concurrent sessions: 180 sessions (peak minute), peak 5-min moving average ~150
- Daily traffic: ~24k requests/day (weekday), weekend ~9k
- Prompt length (tokens): median 72, mean 85, p95 210, p99 380
- Response length (tokens): median 120, mean 280, p95 820, p99 1500
- Streaming usage: ~60% of user-facing generation calls (we stream partial responses to the client)
- Prompts per session: avg 6.8 (users do short back-and-forths)
- Median session duration: 2m 40s
- Daypart: 40% of daily volume in a 2-hour peak window (PST 9–11am)
- KV-cache: estimated cacheable prefix rate 18% (we do some deterministic prompts)
- Models: primarily an Llama-like open model we host with occasional larger backbone for complex queries (we'd like fallback behavior)
- SLOs: p95 first-token <= 250ms, p99 end-to-end <= 1.2s (customer-facing requirement)

Attachments: vectorforge_token_histogram.csv (counts by prompt/response bins).

—Marta
Platform Lead | VectorForge

Subject: Re: Fwd: VectorForge — Dedicated sizing worksheet and traffic profile request

Quick first-pass sketch attached (VectorForge_capacity_sketch.xlsx). Summary below — assumptions and risks included.

Summary estimate (conservative, prefers latency SLOs):
- Target SLOs: p95 first-token <= 250ms, p99 end-to-end <= 1.2s (customer req)
- Model: primary Llama-family 13B quantized (fp16/4-bit mix) for most calls; fallbacks to larger 34B for complex queries (~10% of calls)
- Peak concurrent active generations: 
  - Baseline active token generators at peak minute (accounting for streaming): ~180 sessions * 0.85 active gen fraction = ~153 concurrent generators
  - Accounting for long responses (p99 tokens ~1500) increases effective token-time; for sizing we convert to token-seconds and map to GPU throughput
- GPU SKU suggestion: A100-80GB class or equivalent newer Ampere/Blackwell node for high-throughput mixed workloads; consider 2x H100 per pod if customer requires lower latency on 34B fallback
- Node count (conservative): 6 nodes (A100-equivalent) delivering target throughput + 25% burst headroom for the 2-hour peak (assumes batching + KV-cache 18% reduction)
- Autoscale/burst: allow short-term burst pool of additional 2 nodes (pre-warmed) for sustained peaks > 5 min, with automatic fallback to slightly smaller model variants to preserve latency during saturation

Assumptions & important notes:
- We assume batching efficiency of ~1.6x for their prompt length distribution; streaming reduces batching on streaming calls — treat streaming calls as lower batchability (we assume 0.9x batching multiplier for streaming portion)
- KV-cache 18% reduces token compute proportionally for cached calls; placement of cache (edge vs backend) impacts latency — prefer front-line prefix cache to hit first-token SLOs
- p99 long-tail responses dominate compute cost; recommend soft-response truncation option for some non-critical paths or async worker pool for >1k token outputs to protect latency SLOs
- Network/socket limits: streaming will increase concurrent socket counts; ensure workload proxy has >=2x expected peak sockets (estimate ~350 concurrent sockets at peak)
- Storage/egress: quantify separately if VectorForge offloads embeddings or large artifacts; not included in this sketch

Next steps I recommend we:
1) Validate a small synthetic replay using their token histogram to get measured tokens/sec on suggested SKU.
2) Confirm their fallback model mix (how often to route to 34B).
3) Draft a burst agreement (2-hour guaranteed pre-warm + pay-as-you-go for above) — Camila/Laura to advise on commit band suggested.

Attached: VectorForge_capacity_sketch.xlsx (node counts, throughput model, token-seconds calcs) and vf_preflight_answers.pdf (cleaned copy of Marta's answers).

—Priyom
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
